<MethodEndpoint
  method={'post'}
  path={'/v1/admin/encryption/reencryption'}
  context={'endpoint'}
></MethodEndpoint>

Records a standing request for the background sweep to move every stored onboarding onto the active key, including rows still naming a superseded one. Rotation alone does not do this: it changes which key new writes use and leaves stored rows where they are until something rewrites them. This is the answer to a data key whose material leaked, where those rows must stop naming it without waiting. The work is a batch per sweep tick, each row decrypted and re-encrypted inside one transaction, so no row is ever stored as plain JSON on the way across — unlike turning encryption off and on again, which writes every onboarding to disk unencrypted in between. `progress.pending` counts rows not yet on the active key for as long as the request stands, and the sweep clears it once none are left. Idempotent: asking again while one stands re-stamps it and changes nothing else.
